summary: This defines a RobotPet class that stores a name, a battery level, and a mood, plus a can_walk method that decides whether the pet has enough battery for a walk of a given length. Two pets are then created so the method has something to be tested against.

lines.text: The initializer runs whenever a new RobotPet is created and receives the three values that describe the pet.
Storing the battery level on the object is what later lets can_walk compare it against the energy a walk needs.
This is the behaviour worth testing: it takes a walk length and answers a yes-or-no question about it.

lines.code: """Check if the pet has enough energy for a walk of given duration (in minutes)."""
lines.text: A docstring records the rule the method implements, including the unit of duration, so a reader never has to guess whether it means minutes or hours.
The cost rule is that each minute of walking drains two units of battery.
The comparison produces True or False directly, which is exactly the kind of clear-cut result an assertion can check.
Rover has a healthy battery, so it will serve as the example that should be allowed to walk.
Beep starts with much less charge, giving you a second case that fails for longer walks.
